newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 drops 50 points on rate rise fears.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 drops 50 points on rate rise fears.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index extended its early losses by early afternoon on Tuesday, as prospects for an interest rate rise later this week weighed on sentiment.
The blue chip index was down 51.3 points at 4,759.4 by 1215 GMT, with decliners in a four-to-one majority.
Speculation about a rise in interest rates was given new life after official figures on Tuesday showed a rise in Britain's inflation rate to a higher-than-expected 2.9 percent in the year to June.
Rates were expected to be raised by a quarter point to 6.75 percent by the newly independent Bank of England after a monetary policy meeting starting on Wednesday.

With the pound up again against the mark, there was concern that rising rates together with currency strength would tighten the squeeze on British company profits -- already subject to downgrades in many sectors.

The sharp decline in the FTSE came just two sessions after the index scored a record 4,879.0 in the wake of last week's budget, which many participants believe did not do enough to raise taxes and prevent the economy overheating.
